title: gitapex skill metadata sidecar (SkillMetadata gitapex.io/v1alpha1)
description: Schema for every skills/<name>/metadata/gitapex.yaml sidecar. Kubernetes-CRD-shaped by deliberate convention (apiVersion/kind/metadata/spec envelope) -- never applied to a real cluster; the envelope buys schema versioning (apiVersion), a self-describing kind, and a clean metadata (identity) vs. spec (declared content) split. Structural/type/enum/pattern rules and the single cross-FIELD rule this format has (spec.skillDependencies.requires vs. spec.portability; spec.lifecycle.experimental vs. spec.lifecycle.stable) are expressed here. What this schema deliberately CANNOT express -- and therefore still needs a companion drift scanner, mirroring .gitapex/ssot.schema.json + .github/scripts/scan_ssot_schema.py's own split between jsonschema.Draft202012Validator (this file) and repo-grounded reference-drift checks (the scanner) -- is anything that requires reading a SECOND file: metadata.name equalling the real skill directory name; spec.skillDependencies.requires/relatedTo and spec.lifecycle.deprecated.replacement each resolving to an existing sibling skills/<name>/ directory; and the repo-wide acyclicity of the spec.skillDependencies.requires graph across all sidecars (a single instance has no view of the graph). Also out of scope, permanently, by kind rather than by gap: every check in skills/evaluating-skill-quality/scripts/check_skill_shape.py that inspects SKILL.md/references/*.md prose (bare-issue-number citation scanning, Markdown link/anchor resolution, cross-skill citation resolution, illustrative-model-identifier/placeholder scanning, step-location-contradiction detection, and more) -- those checks are not about this sidecar file's shape at all, and no JSON Schema for metadata/gitapex.yaml can ever cover them.

apiVersion.description: A namespacing string in k8s group/version form, not a claim to own the domain. v1alpha1 signals the schema is still evolving; a future breaking change bumps this, not this file's own $id.

kind.description: The one recognized kind this schema describes.

metadata.description: Identity only, mirroring k8s metadata's role. Every sidecar in this repository today declares only `name`; additionalProperties is false because that is the only field the checker has ever recognized here (unlike k8s's own metadata, which also carries labels/annotations/namespace) -- widen this deliberately, not by accident, if a second field is ever added.

name.description: Must equal the skill's own directory name (skills/<name>/) -- the metadata-name-matches-dir check. That equality is a cross-file fact this schema cannot verify on its own (it never sees the directory a given instance was read from); the companion scanner re-derives it the same way check_skill_shape.py does, from the instance's own file path. The kebab-case pattern here matches this repository's real, already-observed directory-naming convention (NAME_RE in check_skill_shape.py), not a separately gated rule of its own.

spec.description: additionalProperties is deliberately true: check_skill_shape.py's own _parse_manifest docstring states that any spec key other than the six gated ones below (e.g. the reserved-but-ungated spec.evalStatus) is 'still deliberately skipped' -- tolerated, not rejected. Only the six keys enumerated in `properties` below carry a real shape contract; anything else is unenforced free-form space by design, not an oversight.

portability.description: PORTABILITY_LEVELS. Portable: every instruction resolves inside the skill's own directory, vendorable as-is. Mixed/Repository-scoped: at least one instruction legitimately depends on this repository's own paths/conventions.

capabilityAssumption.description: CAPABILITY_ASSUMPTIONS. The compute/capability regime this skill's own verbosity and degree-of-freedom are calibrated for; grades the rubric's dimensions 2/3/9 (and 5, Adaptive-only) relative to this declaration rather than one fixed preference.

references.description: spec.references, if present, must be non-empty (references-well-formed) -- an explicit empty list is not a valid way to say 'no provenance yet'; omit the key entirely instead.

allOf.$comment: requires-portability-compatible: a non-empty spec.skillDependencies.requires is incompatible with spec.portability: Portable -- a Portable skill's own definition (every instruction resolves inside its own directory) contradicts declaring a hard dependency on a sibling skill. This is a genuine cross-FIELD rule (both sides live in the same document), unlike the cross-FILE rules this schema cannot express -- so, unlike those, it belongs here rather than in the companion scanner.

referenceItem.description: One maintainer-facing provenance event (a decision, an audit round, a correction, ...) -- REFERENCES_ITEM_SUBKEYS. Deliberately one event per item, not several fused together (issue #488): an over-budget summary is a decomposition problem, not a length-limit problem.

kind.description: REFERENCES_KIND_VOCAB, a closed vocabulary derived from the entry shapes already in use across every sidecar's spec.references -- not speculative.

anchor.description: The provenance source: a full https://github.com/tvna/gitapex/issues/<N> (or /pull/<N>) URL, another absolute URL, a repo-relative path, or method:<skill-name> for an audit with no dedicated issue. Free-form beyond minLength -- no-bare-issue-citation (a prose scan across the whole sidecar for a bare #N/owner/repo#N token, run by check_skill_shape.py) is deliberately NOT reproduced as a schema pattern here: that scan's real implementation excludes inline code, fenced blocks, and Markdown-link spans with its own multi-hundred-line rule set, and a partial regex reimplementation here would silently diverge from it rather than genuinely cover it. This remains the companion scanner's (or check_skill_shape.py's) job, not this schema's.

summary.description: REFERENCES_ENTRY_MAX_CHARS. The WHAT/WHY of this one event.

outcome.description: Optional, free-form key/value atoms (verdict, found, fixed, before, after, ...) -- no closed vocabulary; real entries use too varied a set of outcome facts for a fixed schema to fit.

skillDependencies.description: The inter-skill dependency graph, split by strength. A key present but holding real YAML null (a bare `skillDependencies:` header with nothing under it) is rejected by the `type: object` constraint above, matching check_skill_shape.py's own null/absent distinction: absent means not declared (valid, optional); present-but-null is a real shape defect (skill-dependencies-well-formed), never silently read as 'declared, nothing inside'.

requires.description: Hard: the procedure cannot function without it. An empty list is a valid, deliberate 'no hard dependencies' statement, unlike spec.references. Every name must resolve to an existing skills/<name>/ directory (skill-dependencies-resolve) -- cross-file, checked by the companion scanner, not this schema. The full requires-graph across all sidecars must also be acyclic (a repo-wide invariant enforced by tests/test_skill_metadata_sidecar.py, entirely outside any single instance's own schema).

relatedTo.description: Soft: boundary/complement/see-also. Same dangling-reference and empty-list rules as requires, but a relatedTo cycle is expected and fine (two independently-usable skills can legitimately point at each other).

lifecycle.description: Migration-lifecycle bookkeeping (Rust/Python/Go/Kubernetes-style entry+exit declarations). Absent entirely means implicitly Stable -- every skill in this repository today. Structured bookkeeping only; it has no rubric grading effect and no skill's own runtime procedure may read or branch on any part of it (the sidecar's behavior-neutrality invariant).

renamedFrom.description: Backward-pointing only: sits on the SURVIVING (new) skill's own sidecar, naming the old, now-nonexistent directory (a `git mv` target). Deliberately NOT resolved against sibling directories, unlike deprecated.replacement -- the whole point is that the old name no longer exists.

not.$comment: experimental-stable-compatible: 'not yet graduated' and 'already graduated on some date' are a real logical contradiction, unlike experimental+deprecated (independent, ungated -- an experimental skill can legitimately be superseded by a different experiment).

trackingIssue.description: A full GitHub issue/PR URL, anchoring the whole string -- deliberately not a bare #123/owner/repo#123 shape (that loses its meaning once this sidecar travels with its skill directory to another repository via vendoring). Shape-only: never resolved against a live GitHub API call, matching check_skill_shape.py's own offline/read-only design.

replacement.description: Must resolve to an existing sibling skills/<name>/ directory (lifecycle-deprecated-replacement-resolves) -- cross-file, checked by the companion scanner, not this schema.

removeAfter.description: Documentation only, per the design's explicit non-goal -- no CI step in this repository deletes a skill once this date passes.

compatibilityGuarantee.description: COMPATIBILITY_GUARANTEE_LEVELS, Kubernetes' own alpha/beta/GA API-stability tiers borrowed as a shape-gated-only enum -- no rule ties this to a sibling's spec.skillDependencies.requires.

lifecycleReason.description: REFERENCES_ENTRY_MAX_CHARS, the same free-text cap spec.references' own summary field uses.

lifecycleDate.description: Strict YYYY-MM-DD, and a real calendar date (e.g. 2026-02-30 must fail, not just fail the shape). The `pattern` alone only gates shape; `format: date` additionally requires a validator run with format assertion enabled (jsonschema.Draft202012Validator(..., format_checker=jsonschema.FormatChecker())) to reject an out-of-range date the same way check_skill_shape.py's own datetime.date.fromisoformat check does -- a schema consumer that ignores format assertions (permitted by the JSON Schema spec itself) only gets the shape check from `pattern`, so the companion scanner MUST enable format checking explicitly, not assume it is on by default.

executionRequirements.description: Only one recognized subkey so far (tools); further categories (filesystem/network/mcp/credentials/browser/externalServices/context) are deferred -- until they land, any key other than tools here is a real unknown key, not reserved space, matching check_skill_shape.py's own current behavior.

executionRequirementsTools.description: Free-form capability tags; this schema (like check_skill_shape.py) does not define a fixed vocabulary for the tag strings themselves.

skillNameRef.description: The same kebab-case shape as metadata.name (NAME_RE) -- every real reference to a sibling skill in this repository is a bare directory-name component, never a path. Constraining the shape here, not just at the companion scanner's own dangling-reference check, closes a real bug an adversarial review found: (skills_dir / entry).is_dir() alone does not defend against an absolute path (pathlib's own '/' operator discards the left operand entirely when the right one is absolute, e.g. Path('/repo/skills') / '/etc' == Path('/etc')) or a '../' traversal segment -- both are schema-valid under a bare `type: string, minLength: 1` constraint, and could make a dangling reference silently read as resolving whenever the escaped path happens to exist. The companion scanner independently guards the same case in code (_is_bare_skill_name) as defense in depth, not as a substitute for this pattern.

toolTagList.description: An explicit empty list is a deliberate 'zero tools of this kind needed' statement, distinct from the key being absent entirely (not yet declared).
